description: Welcome! We are forming a team for the 'Flame in Freefall' challenge. Our goal is to explore microgravity combustion data and develop innovative solutions for space fire safety. We are looking for passionate members with skills in programming, web development, and data analysis to join us and create an impactful project.
summary: AeroFlame is an integrated spacecraft fire safety platform combining a web-based microgravity material analyzer with an autonomous hardware simulation twin. It addresses the microgravity flame challenge by evaluating verified materials, detecting spherical fires, and streaming live telemetry to trigger an H-Bridge reverse braking pulse. This instantly stops ventilation fans and seals dampers at zero centimeters per second, effectively starving the fire of oxygen safely without water. This protects astronaut lives and sensitive equipment during long-duration deep-space missions by mitigating enriched-oxygen hazards and toxic off-gassing.
details:
What it does & How it works:

AeroFlame is a dual-stage spacecraft fire safety system and web-to-hardware digital twin designed for microgravity (0g) and partial-gravity habitats.

Bullet Stage 1 (Pre-Flight Material Screening): A web-based interactive analyzer powered by NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) data (Saffire I–VI, SOFIE, BASS) and NASA-STD-6001. It evaluates 22 spacecraft materials across 4 gravity regimes (ISS, Moon, Mars, Earth), calculating Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI), sample thickness heat-sink effects (0.5–15 mm), flame spread velocity, and toxic off-gassing (CO, HCN, HCl), while recommending safer NASA alternatives like Nomex and PBI/Kevlar.

Bullet Stage 2 (Autonomous Hardware Suppression): When a fire occurs, the web platform streams live JSON telemetry to our hardware prototype. Using dual-sensor verification (temperature + smoke) to prevent space-dust false alarms, the system triggers an L293D H-Bridge reverse-braking pulse. This stops HVAC ventilation fans instantly (0 cm/s airflow) and seals cabin dampers, starving the spherical flame within its own CO2 shell without using water or toxic foam. A mandatory 60-second Cool-Flame Guard lock prevents fan restart until invisible ~300°C cool flames fully extinguish, supported by automated UV camera monitoring.  

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Bullet Eliminates water/foam damage to sensitive spacecraft avionics by using airflow starvation.

Bullet Prevents catastrophic flashovers in enriched-oxygen environments (such as Artemis lunar cabins at 34% O2).

Bullet Protects astronaut lives by calculating exact SCBA breathing mask safety windows and preventing invisible cool-flame re-ignition.  

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software:

Bullet Software & Web: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript ( interactive spherical flame canvas & physics engine), GitHub Pages.

Bullet Hardware & Simulation: Arduino Uno / ESP32, C/C++, L293D H-Bridge Motor Driver, TMP36 / NTC Temperature Sensors, Photoelectric Smoke/Gas Sensors, Servo Motors, LCD Display, Piezo Buzzer, simulated via Wokwi and Tinkercad.

Bullet Data Sources: NASA PSI Repository & NASA-STD-6001.  

Creativity & Factors Considered:

Our team considered the unique physics of microgravity—where thermal buoyancy is absent, causing flames to form floating spheres driven entirely by life-support ventilation. Instead of fighting the fire with heavy suppression agents, we creatively turned the spacecraft's own HVAC system into the primary suppression mechanism via active H-Bridge reverse braking, paired with UV visual verification to detect invisible cool flames before restoring cabin airflow.
